A second page renders a main landmark, which a document may have only one of. Leave `landmarks` at "auto" on pages in a pane or an overlay, or set landmarks="region" on the ones that are not the document's page.
Give this page an `accessible-label`, so it becomes a named region, or landmarks="page" if it holds the main content.
Set `back-text` to the name of the previous pane: on a smaller screen that pane goes away, and this is the way back to it.

This `width` is not supported and is ignored: the popover is an inline-size query container, so its width cannot come from its own content. Give it a CSS length instead.
The sum of the segment values exceeds `max`. Segments are normalized proportionally.

`nldd-drag-handle-cell` is now `nldd-reorder-handle-cell`. Rename the tag, its import and its class, here and on every page.
Bare text or an inline element is a direct child, and each one lands in a column of 0px. Wrap it in a block element such as `p` where the content is made, or put plain text in nldd-text.
Use an nldd-list-item-segment, so the hover looks like the rest of the row and not like a surface on top of it.
Set `decorative`: the row is the checkbox, and this one only shows its state.
End the row with an nldd-icon-cell with icon="chevron-right", which says there is more behind it without the word "openen".
A row is one control: keep one of `href`, `button`, `checkbox` and `radio`.
Use the `text` of an nldd-text-cell: a row is not a heading.
Move the `href` or `button` to a segment: both together put a control in a control.

Keep one action under the form. The way out is `dismiss-text` on the title bar.
A sheet is full height by default and `full-height` does nothing; remove it.
Invalid `height`. Falling back to full height. Use "full", "fit-content", or a valid CSS length (such as "50dvh" or "480px").
Set `dismiss-text` on the title bar, so the sheet has a visible way out.
No `accessible-label` and no nldd-top-title-bar with text inside. Screen readers will announce this dialog with a generic name. Give the title bar a text, or set `accessible-label`.
Put an nldd-title above the form and point `collapse-anchor` at it: the bar stays quiet until the heading scrolls away.
`nldd-app-view` is now `nldd-shell`. Rename the tag, its import and its class, here and on every page.
Set `sidebar-label`: it names the sidebar and titles the sheet it becomes.
Wrap the bar in an nldd-skip-link in `slot="header"`, so a keyboard user can go straight to the content.
No rendered element follows the skip link, so it has nothing to move focus to. Put the content it skips to right after it, or point `href` at the id of the target.
The target did not take focus, so the skip link did nothing. It is probably hidden or inert.

rules.message: The attribute does nothing: the slot for the same content is filled, and what is in the slot wins. Remove one of the two.
nldd-split-button opens one overlay: the one in the `popup` slot, or else the first. Remove the others.
nldd-split-button has no menu, so its chevron opens nothing. Put an nldd-menu or nldd-popover in its `popup` slot, or point `popovertarget` at one.
Only an nldd-menu or nldd-popover goes in nldd-split-button; anything else does not render. Set the label with `text` and the icon with `icon`.
Set landmarks="page" on the page in the pane with the main content, or the screen offers no main landmark or two.
Render nldd-sheet at the document root: as a slotted child it takes the height of the pane, and a sticky footer comes loose.
The status bar sits below a top bar. It belongs above it, as the first thing on the screen.
Set `decorative` on the dot and put the word next to it in an nldd-text-cell: the word carries the meaning.
`current` moved to the step. Set `status="current"` on the current nldd-step-bar-item instead.
`nldd-step-indicator-item` is now `nldd-step-bar-item`. Rename the tag, its import and its class, here and on every page.
More than one step has `status="current"`; the last one wins. Mark only the step you are on.
More than 7 steps do not fit a step bar. Put them under each other in an nldd-list with an nldd-step-cell per row.
`nldd-step-indicator` is now `nldd-step-bar`. Rename the tag, its import and its class, here and on every page.
`text` and `icon` only fit in a full dot on a wide track (`size="md"` with `level="major"`); they are not shown here.
`marker-offset` is not a CSS length or percentage, so the dot falls back to `vertical-alignment`. Use a length such as "1rem" or a percentage such as "25%".
`nldd-timeline-track-cell` is now `nldd-step-cell`. Rename the tag, its import and its class, here and on every page.
The `variant` attribute is now `level`. Rename it here and on every other nldd-step-cell.
Set the look with the attributes of a component, not with style.
A stylesheet of the app's own: the look comes from the components and their attributes.
Add an nldd-breadcrumbs to the footer: a page below the home has a back button and a breadcrumb.
An nldd-swatch-picker-item shows one of `color`, `custom-color` or `image`: an image covers a color, and a category `color` wins over `custom-color`. Keep one.
An nldd-swatch-picker-item with a `custom-color` or an `image` has no accessible name. Add `text`; only a category `color` brings a name of its own.
nldd-swatch-picker needs `accessible-label`, `accessible-labeled-by` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or it has no accessible name.
nldd-switch needs `accessible-label` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or use nldd-switch-field. Without one it has no accessible name.
Tabs with `href` go to another page: add `navigation`, so the bar is a nav with aria-current="page" instead of a tablist, and set `current` on the tab of the page you are on.
`selected` is now `current` and the old attribute does nothing; rename it.
nldd-tab-bar needs `accessible-label`, so a screen reader can say what the tabs are for.
Give the tab bar a high `priority`, so it is the last to move to the overflow.
Give the tab bar an nldd-menu-group in `slot="overflow"`, with a type="radio" item per tab.
nldd-table needs `columns`, a CSS grid track list, or its cells do not line up.
No rows and nothing in [slot="empty"], so the table renders a blank area. Put an nldd-inline-dialog in that slot saying what is not there and what the next move is.
nldd-table needs `accessible-label`: role="table" takes its name from there.
Put the tags below the title, in its slot or after it: the reader needs the subject before the metadata means anything.
An icon-only tag without an `accessible-label` has no accessible name. Add `accessible-label` so screen readers can announce it.
This is not a size the text can use, so it keeps its size from `size` at this breakpoint. Use a length such as "96px" or "6rem", not a keyword.
This custom size is smaller than `display-1` at this breakpoint and shows as `display-1`. Use `size` for text up to `display-1`.
runCommand() got a name that is not a command.
The query of this typeahead is not a valid regular expression; the default is used.
The button in the `button` slot has a size of its own, but the field sets it: `sm` in a field of `md`, `xs` in one of `sm`. Leave the size off the button.

rules.message: nldd-toggle-button-group needs `accessible-label`, `accessible-labeled-by` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or it has no accessible name.

`required` on a checkbox group is announced but not enforced: HTML has no way to say "at least one of these", so the form still submits with nothing selected. Check it yourself on submit, or use radio mode.
nldd-toggle-button with variant="icon" has no `icon` and no slot="icon" content, so a placeholder icon is shown.
nldd-toggle-button needs `text` or `accessible-label`, otherwise it has no accessible name.
Set layout="wrap" on the strip: the default stacks the tokens under each other.
Put the bar with only="sm" after slot="main" in the HTML: on a phone it belongs at the bottom, within reach of a thumb.
Set size="lg" on the bottom bar, which puts the labels under the icons and makes the actions fit next to the sections.
The toolbar overwrites this size with its own. Set `size` on nldd-toolbar, which passes it to every control in it.
Put the toolbar in an nldd-container with padding: the bar split view sets none itself.
Give this item an alternative in `slot="overflow"`: on a narrow screen it moves to the overflow menu, and without one it is gone.
The `label` attribute is now `accessible-label`. Rename it here and on every other nldd-toolbar.
Use a plain button for a single action.
Give the primary action the highest `priority`, so it is the last to move to the overflow.
Give the toolbar item a `min-width` and a `max-width`, so the field shrinks along without becoming unreadable.
Give each toolbar an `accessible-label` when a page has more than one.
Keep the bar to search, language and account: the pages together are the navigation.
Leave `global` empty and let the pages be the navigation: put the entries on the home page as `nldd-card` or `nldd-list`, and keep search and language in `utility`.
`logo-href` and `website-href` go to the same page; leave out `logo-href` so the start page is one link instead of two.
Set content-priority="text", so "Zoeken" and "NL" stay readable on a narrow screen.

`collapse-anchor` points at an element that is no heading and holds none. The bar keeps its own title as the heading, so the page has one, but a screen reader now finds the title twice. Point the anchor at the nldd-title that starts the content.
`collapse-anchor` matches nothing yet. If it never renders, the bar keeps its own title and reads it out twice.

This item has a rule of its own and is also named in `unmet`. The rule decides, and the name is ignored: it is a snapshot of the previous check and cannot be newer than the value. Drop it from `unmet`, or take the rule off the item.
